cards.title: The Ground + Press Drop
cards.invitation: Reconnect with support. Regulate from the ground up.
cards.purpose: Grounding & bodily support. Feel where you are. Use what supports you.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Stand with both feet on the floor. Let your knees be soft and notice the contact beneath your feet.

practiceSteps.label: Press
practiceSteps.instruction: Place your palms on a stable surface, such as a wall or countertop. Press gently — not as hard as you can.

practiceSteps.label: Feel
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice the pressure beneath your palms and through the soles of your feet. Feel the surface meeting you.

practiceSteps.label: Receive
practiceSteps.instruction: Allow some of your body weight to be supported by the floor and the surface. You don't need to hold yourself up through effort alone.

practiceSteps.label: Pause
practiceSteps.instruction: Stay for a few slow breaths. Notice your feet, hands, posture, and the space your body occupies.

practiceSteps.label: Release
practiceSteps.instruction: Gradually soften the pressure through your hands. Keep your feet connected to the floor and notice what changes.

whatToNotice.text: Pressure — What do you feel where your hands and feet make contact?
Position — Can you sense where your body is in space?
Support — What changes when you allow the surface to hold some of your weight?

cards.gentleNote: Move at your own pace. Use a stable, secure surface. This practice can be adapted to sitting if needed. If you experience pain or dizziness, reduce the pressure or take a break.
cards.anchor: I have weight. I can create pressure. I can be supported.

cards.title: The Heel Press Reset
cards.invitation: Find support through your feet.
cards.purpose: Grounding & bodily support. Feel where you are. Use what supports you.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Stand with both feet on the floor. Let your awareness settle in your lower body.

practiceSteps.label: Focus
practiceSteps.instruction: Bring your specific awareness to your heels. Notice their position and contact.

practiceSteps.label: Gentle Press
practiceSteps.instruction: Gradually and gently increase pressure of both heels into the floor.

practiceSteps.label: Sense
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice the firm, supportive feeling directly beneath each heel.

practiceSteps.label: Breathe
practiceSteps.instruction: Take two slow breaths, maintaining this gentle heel press.

practiceSteps.label: Release
practiceSteps.instruction: Slowly release the extra pressure, keeping your heels connected to the floor.

whatToNotice.text: Pressure — What do you feel when your heels make contact?
Position — Can you sense the exact location of your heels?
Support — What changes when you let the floor hold your heel weight?

cards.gentleNote: Move at your own pace. Use a stable, secure surface to steady yourself if needed. This practice should not cause pain. If you experience pain, dizziness, or sharp discomfort, stop immediately.
cards.anchor: I can feel the ground beneath me.

cards.title: The Four-Point Foot Map
cards.invitation: Notice how your feet meet the ground.
cards.purpose: Foot awareness & bodily orientation. (Feel where you stand. Understand your foundation.)

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Take a comfortable standing stance, feet hip-width apart. Settle your weight evenly.

practiceSteps.label: Heel Point
practiceSteps.instruction: Find the point under the center of your heel. Feel its dense contact with the ground.

practiceSteps.label: Outer Point
practiceSteps.instruction: Locate the outer edge, near the ball of your pinky toe. Shift weight slightly to sense its edge.

practiceSteps.label: Inner Point
practiceSteps.instruction: Sense the point at the ball of your big toe. Notice its unique shape and pressure.

practiceSteps.label: Toe Pads
practiceSteps.instruction: Feel the soft cushions of all ten toe pads. Wiggle them to engage, then rest.

practiceSteps.label: Merge Points
practiceSteps.instruction: Bring all four points—heel, outer edge, inner edge, and toe pads—into unified, stable contact. Breathe and feel the map.

whatToNotice.text: Distribution — Are all four points equally weighted?
Position — How does clearer foot contact affect your overall alignment?
Support — Do your feet feel like reliable anchors for your body?

cards.gentleNote: Move at your own pace. Ensure you are on a stable, level surface. The practice can be adapted to sitting. Adjust your stance if you feel discomfort.
cards.anchor: I can feel where I stand.

cards.title: The Wall Support Press
cards.invitation: Meet support with your own pressure.
cards.purpose: Support, pressure & physical orientation. Feel where you are. Use what supports you.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Stand with both feet on floor. Relax knees.

practiceSteps.label: Press
practiceSteps.instruction: Place palms flat on wall at shoulder height. Press firmly.

practiceSteps.label: Feel
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice wall pressure beneath palms & ground support under feet.

practiceSteps.label: Receive
practiceSteps.instruction: Allow the wall to share the task of supporting your structure.

practiceSteps.label: Pause
practiceSteps.instruction: Take slow breaths. Sense your body's shape & position.

practiceSteps.label: Release
practiceSteps.instruction: Gradually decrease pressure in your palms. Stay connected.

whatToNotice.text: Pressure — What do you feel where your palms make contact?
Location — Can you sense your position relative to the wall?
Meet — Notice how your pressure is met by the wall.

cards.gentleNote: Move at your own pace. Use a stable wall. Adapt to sitting if needed. Lessen pressure if discomfort occurs.
cards.anchor: I can meet support with my own strength.

cards.title: The Chair Support Drop
cards.invitation: Reconnect with support, let your body receive support.
cards.purpose: Seated grounding & bodily support. Feel the chair beneath you. Allow yourself to be held.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Sit back into the chair, feet flat on the floor. Let your hips settle.

practiceSteps.label: Press
practiceSteps.instruction: Place your hands on your lap or the chair arms. Apply gentle pressure.

practiceSteps.label: Feel
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice the texture and support of the chair back and seat against your body.

practiceSteps.label: Receive
practiceSteps.instruction: Allow the chair to fully support your weight. You don't need to hold yourself up.

practiceSteps.label: Pause
practiceSteps.instruction: Stay for a few slow breaths. Notice your points of contact and your breathing.

practiceSteps.label: Release
practiceSteps.instruction: Gradually soften any postural effort. Stay connected to the support and notice what changes.

whatToNotice.text: Pressure — What do you feel where your back, seat, and feet make contact?
Position — Can you sense your body's relation to the chair and the ground?
Support — What changes when you fully trust the chair to hold your weight?

cards.gentleNote: This practice can be done in any stable chair. If you experience discomfort, adjust your position or take a break.
cards.anchor: I can receive support and remain present.

cards.title: The Back-Body Anchor
cards.invitation: Feel what is supporting you from behind.
cards.purpose: Back-body awareness & physical support. Feel what is behind you. Lean into existing support.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Sit comfortably in the chair. Let your feet rest flat on the floor.

practiceSteps.label: Lean
practiceSteps.instruction: Gently lean your back into the chair. Notice the contact of your spine.

practiceSteps.label: Feel
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice the pressure points along your back and shoulders. Can you soften into this pressure?

practiceSteps.label: Receive
practiceSteps.instruction: Allow the chair to carry some of your body weight. Relinquish the effort of holding yourself up.

practiceSteps.label: Pause
practiceSteps.instruction: Stay for a few slow breaths. Check in with your breath and body's position.

practiceSteps.label: Release
practiceSteps.instruction: Gradually soften the tension in your back muscles. Maintain the contact without force.

whatToNotice.text: Pressure — What do you feel where your back makes contact with the chair?
Position — Can you sense the position of your spine and shoulders in relation to the chair?
Support — What changes when you allow the chair to take some of your back-body weight?

cards.gentleNote: Move at your own pace. Ensure the chair is stable and secure. This practice can be adapted for standing if needed. If you feel discomfort, reduce the pressure or take a break.
cards.anchor: There is support behind me.

cards.title: The Weight Shift
cards.invitation: Notice how your weight moves through your feet.
cards.purpose: Weight awareness & postural organisation. Feel the change. Align your center.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Stand with natural posture, feet hip-width. Notice the ground beneath you.

practiceSteps.label: Shift (A)
practiceSteps.instruction: Slowly move your body's weight towards your right foot. Observe the sensation on the inner arch.

practiceSteps.label: Feel
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice the entire footprint. Try to keep toes relaxed and not gripping.

practiceSteps.label: Shift (B)
practiceSteps.instruction: Move weight back through center and then smoothly to the left foot.

practiceSteps.label: Pause & Breathe
practiceSteps.instruction: Hold the position, taking a calm breath. How does balance feel in this spot?

practiceSteps.label: Settle
practiceSteps.instruction: Gradually move weight back to center, allowing your whole body to find a soft, centered state.

whatToNotice.text: Pressure — Where is the weight? Inner edge, heel, or ball of your foot?
Position — Can you sense the precise moment your weight moves?
Support — How does each foot feel to support you? More or less stable?

cards.gentleNote: This is a subtle, internal practice. Move gently and do not force the shift. Maintain upright posture throughout. Pause if you feel unbalanced.
cards.anchor: I can shift and find my centre again.

cards.title: The Midline Press
cards.purpose: Midline awareness & bodily organisation.
cards.orientation: Meet your centre with steady pressure.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Establish a steady, grounded stance. Feel your feet.

practiceSteps.label: Press
practiceSteps.instruction: Bring your palms together, fingers up, at the chest center. Apply steady pressure.

practiceSteps.label: Feel
practiceSteps.instruction: Sense the symmetry, force, and warmth of your meeting palms.

practiceSteps.label: Organise
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice how this central connection organises your core and breath.

practiceSteps.label: Maintain
practiceSteps.instruction: Hold the steady pressure and breathe deeply for several counts.

practiceSteps.label: Release
practiceSteps.instruction: Gently relax palm pressure, while keeping the midline sense present.

whatToNotice.text: Pressure — What changes in your physical sense of self from the midline press?
Position — Can you perceive the core midline of your body from head to pelvis?
Support — How does this practice provide internal structure and support?

cards.gentleNote: Adapt pressure for comfort. Practice at your own pace. If pain occurs, reduce intensity or stop.
cards.anchor: I can meet myself at the centre.

cards.title: The Seated Grounding Press
cards.invitation: Feel your feet while you are supported.
cards.purpose: Seated grounding & lower-body pressure awareness. Feel where you are. Use what supports you.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Sit tall with both feet flat on the floor.

practiceSteps.label: Press
practiceSteps.instruction: Rest your hands comfortably in your lap. Focus your attention on your feet.

practiceSteps.label: Feel
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice the exact sensation of the floor beneath your bare feet.

practiceSteps.label: Receive
practiceSteps.instruction: Allow your weight to settle into the chair, and let the floor completely support your feet.

practiceSteps.label: Pause
practiceSteps.instruction: Stay for a few slow breaths. Notice your feet, your seat in the chair, and the floor.

practiceSteps.label: Release
practiceSteps.instruction: Gradually soften any holding in your body, keeping your feet gently connected.

whatToNotice.text: Pressure — What do you feel where your feet make contact with the floor?
Position — Can you sense the position of your lower legs and feet?
Support — What changes when you allow the chair to hold your upper body and the floor to hold your lower body?

cards.gentleNote: Move at your own pace. This practice can be done at a desk or table. Use a stable, secure surface. If you experience pain or dizziness, take a break.
cards.anchor: I can press down and still be supported.

cards.title: The Axial Alignment Reset
cards.invitation: Find your length without forcing your posture. Regulate from the axial spine out.
cards.purpose: Postural awareness & whole-body organisation. Find your centered length and integrated structure.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Stand with both feet parallel, hip-width apart. Settle into the floor.

practiceSteps.label: Sense
practiceSteps.instruction: Draw your attention from your feet upwards through your legs and pelvis.

practiceSteps.label: Lengthen
practiceSteps.instruction: Quietly imagine a soft string lifting the crown of your head, easing your spine into length.

practiceSteps.label: Release
practiceSteps.instruction: Scan your body for any rigidity and consciously let it go, especially in the neck and shoulders.

practiceSteps.label: Balance
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice how your center of gravity self-adjusts without forceful holding.

practiceSteps.label: Breathe
practiceSteps.instruction: Integration. Savor several natural breaths in this new feeling of space.

whatToNotice.text: Pressure — What do you feel where your hands and feet make contact?
Position — Can you sense where your body is in space?
Support — What changes when you allow the surface to hold some of your weight?

cards.gentleNote: Move at your own pace. Use a stable, secure surface. This practice can be adapted to sitting if needed. If you experience pain or dizziness, reduce the pressure or take a break.
cards.anchor: I can be upright without holding myself rigid.

cards.title: The Physiological Sigh
cards.invitation: Let your breath complete itself.
cards.purpose: Breath recovery & respiratory awareness. Explore a natural two-part inhale followed by a longer, easy exhale. The practice brings attention to the changing shape and rhythm of your breath without asking you to breathe as deeply or forcefully as possible.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Sit or stand comfortably. Let your shoulders and jaw rest naturally and notice your breathing without changing it.

practiceSteps.label: First Inhale
practiceSteps.instruction: Take a comfortable inhale through your nose. Keep the breath easy rather than deliberately making it large.

practiceSteps.label: Second Inhale
practiceSteps.instruction: At the top of the inhale, gently add a small second sip of air if it feels comfortable. Keep this subtle and unforced.

practiceSteps.label: Longer Exhale
practiceSteps.instruction: Allow the breath to leave slowly through your mouth. Let the exhale be easy rather than pushing the air out.

practiceSteps.label: Pause
practiceSteps.instruction: After the exhale, allow your breathing to return naturally. Notice whether your next breath arrives without needing to control it.

practiceSteps.label: Repeat or Stop
practiceSteps.instruction: Repeat for a few comfortable rounds, or simply return to natural breathing. You do not need to complete a set number of repetitions.

whatToNotice.text: Rhythm — What changes between the two-part inhale and the longer exhale?
Effort — Can you keep the breath comfortable rather than making it bigger?
Recovery — What happens when you stop directing the breath and allow it to continue naturally?

cards.gentleNote: This practice does not need to involve a large inhale. If you notice air hunger, dizziness, anxiety or discomfort, return to your natural breathing or stop. Breath-focused practices can feel activating for some people.
cards.anchor: I can let my breath complete itself.

cards.title: The Extended Exhale
cards.invitation: Give your exhale a little more time.
cards.purpose: Breath pacing & recovery. Notice the natural rhythm of your breath. Invite the exhale to complete.

practiceSteps.label: Find Your Seat
practiceSteps.instruction: Stand with both feet on the floor. Or sit with feet on floor and spine supported.

practiceSteps.label: Rest Your Hands
practiceSteps.instruction: Place one hand on your chest and the other on your lower ribs.

practiceSteps.label: Inhale Slowly
practiceSteps.instruction: Take a slow, gentle breath in through your nose.

practiceSteps.label: Begin the Exhale
practiceSteps.instruction: Allow the air to leave softly, perhaps through slightly pursed lips.

practiceSteps.label: Slow It Down
practiceSteps.instruction: Count as you exhale, making it last 2-3 seconds longer than the inhale.

practiceSteps.label: Pause & Notice
practiceSteps.instruction: Feel the end of the exhale. Notice any sense of relaxation or grounding.

whatToNotice.text: Ribcage Motion — Notice the expansion under your hands.
Muscle Tension — Notice any softening in shoulders and neck.
State — Notice any feelings of calmness or settling.

cards.gentleNote: Move at your own pace. If you feel lightheaded, return to a natural rhythm. This practice can be modified for any position. Discontinue if you feel strain.
cards.anchor: I can give myself more time to exhale.

cards.title: The Rib Expansion Reset
cards.invitation: Notice your breath moving through your ribs.
cards.purpose: Rib awareness & respiratory movement. Feel the space your ribs create. Use your hands to sense movement.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Find a comfortable, upright seated position. Let your sit bones anchor and notice your overall posture.

practiceSteps.label: Hand Placement
practiceSteps.instruction: Place your hands gently around your lower side and back ribs. Feel the connection.

practiceSteps.label: Focus
practiceSteps.instruction: Direct your attention to the feeling of air entering your body. Don't change anything yet, just notice.

practiceSteps.label: Breathing In
practiceSteps.instruction: As you inhale, can you feel your ribs expand outward into your hands? Notice the three-dimensional movement (forward, side, back).

practiceSteps.label: Breathing Out
practiceSteps.instruction: As you exhale, notice the gentle softening and return to center. Feel the ribcage move back.

practiceSteps.label: Gentle Release
practiceSteps.instruction: Gradually reduce the hands-on focus but keep the awareness. Continue to breathe with this expanded sensation.

whatToNotice.text: Ribcage Movement — What direction does your ribcage move as you breathe? Can you sense all sides?
Chest vs. Diaphragm — Can you feel the difference between a high chest breath and a lower rib expansion?
Internal Space — How much space does your breath create? What changes when you breathe fully into your ribs?

cards.gentleNote: Move at your own pace. There is no 'right' amount of expansion. This practice can also be done while standing or lying down. If you feel dizzy, reduce the depth of your breath or take a break.
cards.anchor: I can notice my breath without forcing it.

cards.title: The Back-Rib Breath
cards.invitation: Notice the breath you cannot see.
cards.purpose: Posterior rib awareness & breath location. Feel the movement of breath behind you. Use your hands to sense the invisible.

practiceSteps.label: Seat
practiceSteps.instruction: Sit comfortably and tall on a stool. Keep feet flat on the floor.

practiceSteps.label: Place
practiceSteps.instruction: Place your hands around your back ribs, fingers spread, just below the shoulder blades.

practiceSteps.label: Feel (Hands)
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice the warmth and contact of your hands on your back body.

practiceSteps.label: Breath (Gentle)
practiceSteps.instruction: Inhale gently, noticing where your breath naturally flows, without forcing anything.

practiceSteps.label: Invite
practiceSteps.instruction: With patience, observe if breath can be gently invited to expand into the area under your hands.

practiceSteps.label: Observe
practiceSteps.instruction: Allow several soft breaths. Feel any subtle movement in your back ribs and spine.

whatToNotice.text: Breath Pathway — How does the breath flow? Up-and-down, or back-and-forth?
Back Expansion — Do you feel a sense of widening or pushing back?
Spine Alignment — Does breath affect the subtle alignment of your spine?

cards.gentleNote: Go at your own pace. There is no right way. Focus on gentle sensation. Do not force movement. If you experience strain, ease off and rest.
cards.anchor: I can notice what is happening behind me.

cards.title: The Pursed-Lip Exhale
cards.invitation: Let the exhale leave slowly.
cards.purpose: Exhale pacing & breath control. Regulate airflow and CO2.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Find a comfortable posture. Sense your breath.

practiceSteps.label: Inhale
practiceSteps.instruction: Take a normal, deep breath through your nose.

practiceSteps.label: Purse
practiceSteps.instruction: Gently purse your lips, as if for a slow whistle.

practiceSteps.label: Exhale
practiceSteps.instruction: Let the air leave slowly and evenly through pursed lips.

practiceSteps.label: Notice
practiceSteps.instruction: Feel the controlled resistance and gentle pressure.

practiceSteps.label: Regulate
practiceSteps.instruction: Extend the duration of your exhale relative to your inhale.

whatToNotice.text: Breath Cadence — Observe the rhythm and duration.
Airflow — Feel the slow, even flow.
Diaphragm Engagement — Notice the core support.

cards.gentleNote: Move at your own pace. This practice can be done lying down. If you experience dizziness, pause and breathe normally.
cards.anchor: I can let the breath leave slowly.

cards.title: The Hand-on-Ribs Reset
cards.invitation: Feel your breath through your hands.
cards.purpose: Respiratory awareness & breath rhythm. Feel where your body expands. Use your hands for feedback.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Sit comfortably. Find a supported position on a chair or the floor. Let your feet rest.

practiceSteps.label: Place
practiceSteps.instruction: Bring your hands to your ribcage. Rest your palms gently on the lower sides of your ribs.

practiceSteps.label: Inhale
practiceSteps.instruction: Breathe naturally. Feel the ribs expand outward into your hands.

practiceSteps.label: Exhale
practiceSteps.instruction: Let the breath go. Feel the ribs move inward, away from your hands.

practiceSteps.label: Rhythm
practiceSteps.instruction: Track the natural pause. Is it after the inhale, or after the exhale?

practiceSteps.label: Regulate
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice the pace. Is it faster or slower than you expected?

whatToNotice.text: Expansion — Can you feel the breath moving horizontally and vertically?
Texture — What is the surface of your ribcage, the fabric, and your hands like?
Rhythm — Where in the cycle do your hands move the most?

cards.gentleNote: The goal is not to change your breath, but to observe it. If you feel dizzy, return to normal breathing and remove your hands.
cards.anchor: I can feel my breath without controlling it.

cards.title: The Breath Pace Reset
cards.invitation: Find a breathing rhythm you can stay with.
cards.purpose: Breath pacing & predictability. Feel the stability of a steady, calm rhythm.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Sit comfortably. Feel the chair supporting you. Notice your body position.

practiceSteps.label: Observe Inhale
practiceSteps.instruction: Breathe in naturally. Follow the path of the air into your lungs.

practiceSteps.label: Observe Exhale
practiceSteps.instruction: Let the breath go. Notice the sensation of air leaving your body.

practiceSteps.label: Notice Rhythm
practiceSteps.instruction: Count the duration of your natural inhale and exhale for a few cycles.

practiceSteps.label: Gentle Counting
practiceSteps.instruction: Try a simple, comfortable rhythm, e.g., count 4 for inhale, count 4 for exhale.

practiceSteps.label: Stabilize
practiceSteps.instruction: Maintain this predictable count for 5 minutes. Find predictability.

whatToNotice.text: Depth — Where in your body does the breath move? Can you feel it low in your ribs?
Rhythm — Is your counted rhythm steady? Does it feel comfortable and predictable?
Ease — How does your body feel with the paced breathing? Does tension or comfort increase?

cards.gentleNote: Go at your own pace. The goal is predictable rhythm, not lung capacity. Use a count that feels truly comfortable. Return to natural breathing if you experience any lightheadedness.
cards.anchor: I can find a rhythm I can stay with.

cards.title: The Exhale-and-Drop
cards.invitation: Let the exhale invite a little less effort.
cards.purpose: Exhale awareness & muscular softening. Feel your body let go with each breath.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Stand naturally, shoulders back, arms loose, near a softly lit window. Notice the ground beneath your feet.

practiceSteps.label: Exhale
practiceSteps.instruction: Take a long, natural, unforced exhale. Feel your body sink slightly into the support of your skeletal structure.

practiceSteps.label: Drop
practiceSteps.instruction: As you exhale, let your shoulders subtly lower and your ribcage compress without forcing.

practiceSteps.label: Sense
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice lingering tension in areas like your jaw, hands, or abdomen, and allow them to soften.

practiceSteps.label: Repeat
practiceSteps.instruction: Do this for several breath cycles, emphasizing the complete exhale.

practiceSteps.label: Release
practiceSteps.instruction: Finally, allow your whole body to hold less effort, standing naturally and softly, not rigidly.

whatToNotice.text: Pressure — What do you feel where your hands and feet make contact?
Position — Can you sense where your body is in space?
Support — What changes when you allow the surface to hold some of your weight?

cards.gentleNote: Move at your own pace. Use a stable, secure surface. This practice can be adapted to sitting if needed. If you experience pain or dizziness, reduce the pressure or take a break.
cards.anchor: I can soften without forcing myself to relax.

cards.title: The Completion Exhale
cards.invitation: Let one breath finish before the next begins.
cards.purpose: Breath completion & respiratory awareness. Notice the full excursion of your exhale. Discover the silent space between.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Find a comfortable seated position. Place a hand lightly on your ribs.

practiceSteps.label: Observe
practiceSteps.instruction: Allow a slow, natural inhale to come. Feel the ribs expand gently.

practiceSteps.label: Exhale
practiceSteps.instruction: Let the exhale begin smoothly. Focus inward and notice the movement.

practiceSteps.label: Complete
practiceSteps.instruction: Observe the feeling of the exhale coming to a natural end.

practiceSteps.label: Pause
practiceSteps.instruction: Wait for a moment in the space after the exhale. Notice stillness.

practiceSteps.label: Receive
practiceSteps.instruction: Allow the next inhale to arrive on its own impulse. Do not rush.

whatToNotice.text: Ribs — What do you feel under your hand on your ribs?
Time — Can you sense the brief moment after the exhale?
Air Flow — What changes when you allow your breath its full expression?

cards.gentleNote: Go at your own pace. This practice can be adapted to lying down. If you feel lightheaded, return to normal breathing.
cards.anchor: I can let one breath finish before the next begins.

cards.title: The Breath Location Scan
cards.invitation: Notice where your breath moves today.
cards.purpose: Breath location & interoceptive awareness. Notice where the breath is felt. Track its path.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Seated comfortably with your back supported. Close your eyes or soften your gaze.

practiceSteps.label: Inhale
practiceSteps.instruction: Begin a slow, deep inhale. Where do you feel it first?

practiceSteps.label: Trace
practiceSteps.instruction: Mentally track the air as it moves down the trachea and into the lungs.

practiceSteps.label: Expand
practiceSteps.instruction: Identify which areas expand: chest, abdomen, ribcage, or back.

practiceSteps.label: Exhale
practiceSteps.instruction: Note the feeling of release and contraction as you slowly exhale.

practiceSteps.label: Observe
practiceSteps.instruction: What is the rhythm and depth? Do not change it, just notice.

whatToNotice.text: Chest — Where can you feel your chest move?
Abdomen — Is your belly moving, and how?
Ribcage — Can you feel your ribcage expand laterally?

cards.gentleNote: Move at your own pace. Use a comfortable, supportive chair. Maintain soft gaze or keep eyes closed. Adapt to sitting or lying if needed. If you experience any strain, lightheadedness, or discomfort, reduce breath depth or pause the practice.
cards.anchor: I can notice what is here without needing to change it.

cards.title: The Horizon Lock
cards.invitation: Find a steady point in the space around you.
cards.purpose: Visual orientation & present-time location. Choose a stable point in your environment and allow your eyes to rest there. Use the visual reference to notice where you are and how your body exists within the space around you.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Sit or stand in a comfortable position. Let your head rest naturally and allow your eyes to move around the room briefly.

practiceSteps.label: Choose a Point
practiceSteps.instruction: Find one stable visual reference in front of you — a doorway, edge of a window, piece of furniture, or another stationary object.

practiceSteps.label: Let Your Eyes Rest
practiceSteps.instruction: Allow your gaze to settle on the chosen point. Keep the gaze comfortable rather than intense or fixed.

practiceSteps.label: Notice the Space Around It
practiceSteps.instruction: While keeping the point available to your vision, notice what exists around it. Let nearby shapes, light, colours and edges remain part of your awareness.

practiceSteps.label: Locate Yourself
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice where your body is in relation to the visual point. Feel your feet, the chair beneath you or the surface supporting you.

practiceSteps.label: Look Away
practiceSteps.instruction: Allow your eyes to move naturally around the room again. Notice whether your sense of the space has changed.

whatToNotice.text: Location — Where are you in relation to what you are looking at?
Stability — What happens when one visual reference remains available?
Space — Can you notice the surrounding environment as well as the point itself?

cards.gentleNote: There is no need to stare or keep your eyes completely still. Let your gaze move whenever it wants to. If visual focus creates strain, dizziness, headache or discomfort, soften your gaze or look around the room naturally.
cards.anchor: I can find my place in the space around me.

cards.title: The Orienting Sweep
cards.invitation: Orientation: let your eyes discover the space around you.
cards.purpose: Environmental orientation & attentional flexibility. Feel visually connected and aware. Use sight to regulate your state.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Stand or sit comfortably, eyes open. Notice the environment.

practiceSteps.label: Begin
practiceSteps.instruction: Choose a starting point and slowly turn your head.

practiceSteps.label: Scan
practiceSteps.instruction: Allow your eyes to travel across a wall, ceiling, or floor.

practiceSteps.label: Notice
practiceSteps.instruction: Without analyzing, just notice objects, colors, and shapes.

practiceSteps.label: Expand
practiceSteps.instruction: Let your focus widen to take in more of the room.

practiceSteps.label: Pause
practiceSteps.instruction: Stop and rest your gaze on one specific item.

practiceSteps.label: Release
practiceSteps.instruction: Gently look away from that item and continue the sweep or stop.

whatToNotice.text: Perception — What visual details are most immediate?
Depth & Space — How far can you look? Can you sense the room's volume?
Comfort — Which object feels most neutral or pleasant to look at?

cards.gentleNote: Move at your own pace. This practice can be adapted to any posture. If you feel dizzy, reduce the speed of the sweep or take a break.
cards.anchor: I can look around and notice what is here.

cards.title: The Peripheral Vision Reset
cards.invitation: Cultivate visual flexibility. Notice what's around you without looking directly.
cards.purpose: Softening visual focus & widening attention.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Settle your body into a comfortable, relaxed posture. Soften your shoulders.

practiceSteps.label: Soften Gaze
practiceSteps.instruction: Find a point in front of you but let your vision relax. Do not "look" hard.

practiceSteps.label: Widen Periphery
practiceSteps.instruction: Keeping your soft gaze forward, begin to invite visual input from the very edge of your vision.

practiceSteps.label: Notice Details
practiceSteps.instruction: Without moving your eyes, can you perceive the shape or color of an object to your far left?

practiceSteps.label: Feel the Field
practiceSteps.instruction: Sense the entire visual field as a whole, rather than picking out specific objects.

practiceSteps.label: Allow the Space
practiceSteps.instruction: Remain in this state for a few breaths. Notice the felt sense of expanded space.

whatToNotice.text: Scope — How broad is your perceived visual field?
Tension — Is there less tension in your eyes or facial muscles?
Connection — Do you feel more aware of the overall room and yourself in it?

cards.gentleNote: Approach this gently. If your vision feels strained or you get dizzy, simply rest and close your eyes. This is about softening, not forcing.
cards.anchor: My attention can widen without losing where I am.
cards.reviewNote: Artwork's own eyebrow label reads 'SUPPORT, FOCUS, & AWARENESS' rather than the standard 'ORIENTATION & VISUAL-SPATIAL ATTENTION' used on every other Series 03 card - the subtitle line beneath the title and the badge number ('03') both confirm Series 03, so this is treated as a labeling inconsistency in the artwork, not a series-assignment ambiguity. Flagged for awareness.

cards.title: The Near–Far Focus Shift
cards.invitation: Recenter your perception. Adapt your vision from the inside out.
cards.purpose: Orientation & attention flexibility. Feel your eyes and vision adapt. Experience environmental connection.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Find a comfortable seated position near a window.

practiceSteps.label: Choose Near Object
practiceSteps.instruction: Identify a close object like a plant leaf or book edge. Let your gaze land on it.

practiceSteps.label: Study Details
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice the texture, color, and sharp lines. See it clearly without tension.

practiceSteps.label: Choose Far Object
practiceSteps.instruction: Select a distant object outside like a tree branch or building detail.

practiceSteps.label: Shift Focus
practiceSteps.instruction: Softly move your gaze to the distant object. Let the near object become soft.

practiceSteps.label: Appreciate Depth
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice the distance. Can you perceive the space between you and it?

practiceSteps.label: Return Near
practiceSteps.instruction: Bring your attention back to the near object. Allow it to come into sharp focus again.

practiceSteps.label: Repeating
practiceSteps.instruction: Gently cycle your focus 3-5 times, noticing the transitions.

whatToNotice.text: Eye Effort — What sensation do you feel in your eye muscles when shifting?
Depth Perception — Can you sense the spatial relationship between near and far?
Detail Notice — How do textures and colors seem different between points of focus?

cards.gentleNote: Move at your own pace. If your eyes feel strained, soften your gaze or close them for a moment. This practice is about ease, not forced effort. Adapt as needed.
cards.anchor: My attention can move between here and there.

cards.title: The Horizontal Eye Sweep
cards.invitation: Regulate the nervous system with controlled visual scanning.
cards.purpose: Orientation & spatial awareness. Feel where you are visually. Connect to your environment.

practiceSteps.label: Seat & Stabilize
practiceSteps.instruction: Sit comfortably on a chair. Place both feet flat on the floor. Feel your sit bones and let your posture be relaxed yet upright.

practiceSteps.label: Soften Gaze
practiceSteps.instruction: Briefly close your eyes or soften your gaze straight ahead. Release tension around the eyes.

practiceSteps.label: Find Horizon
practiceSteps.instruction: Imagine a soft, horizontal line at eye level in front of you. This is your scanning plane.

practiceSteps.label: Right Sweep
practiceSteps.instruction: Gently and slowly sweep your eyes to the far right, taking in the scene without moving your head. Pause for one soft breath.

practiceSteps.label: Return Center
practiceSteps.instruction: Slowly return your gaze to the center line. Pause.

practiceSteps.label: Left Sweep
practiceSteps.instruction: Repeat the sweep gently to the far left, taking in the scene without moving your head. Pause for one soft breath.

practiceSteps.label: Full Cycle
practiceSteps.instruction: Perform a complete smooth cycle from the center to the right, then center to the left, and back to center.

practiceSteps.label: Re-Orient
practiceSteps.instruction: Stop. Close your eyes for a moment. Then open them, looking all around the room naturally. Notice any changes.

whatToNotice.text: Visual Field — What do you see at the far edges? How wide is your range?
Motion & Stillness — Are you moving your head? Are your eyes tracking smoothly?
Sensation — Notice any changes in tension in your neck, face, or chest.

cards.gentleNote: Practice in a room with varied objects for visual richness. If you feel dizzy, slow down or take a break.
cards.anchor: I can look from side to side and stay connected to the space around me.
cards.reviewNote: The card's own step numbering is inconsistent (shows 01-06 then '07.' with step 8 rendered as a separate side callout rather than in the main list) - all 8 step instructions were transcribed and re-numbered sequentially 0-7 here; a 'Left Sweep' step (labeled step 6 above) is implied by the practice's own symmetry description but its instruction text had to be inferred from the 'Full Cycle' step's own description of a left-then-center movement, since the artwork's step list skips directly from 'Right Sweep'/'Return Center' to 'Full Cycle' without its own explicit 'Left Sweep' line. Flagged for human verification against the original source.

cards.title: The Colour Orientation Reset
cards.invitation: Let colour help you notice what is actually around you.
cards.purpose: Environmental orientation & attentional flexibility. Feel where you are. See what surrounds you.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Stand with both feet on the floor. Let your knees be soft and notice the contact beneath your feet.

practiceSteps.label: Soften Gaze
practiceSteps.instruction: Allow your eyes to rest gently, softening your overall gaze. Don't focus on any one thing.

practiceSteps.label: Scan The Space
practiceSteps.instruction: Begin to slowly look around the room, keeping your neck and jaw relaxed.

practiceSteps.label: Choose A Colour
practiceSteps.instruction: Allow your eyes to find and settle on one primary color in your environment (e.g., a blue vase or red book).

practiceSteps.label: Observe The Shade
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice the specific hue, shade, texture, and how light interacts with that color.

practiceSteps.label: Repeat
practiceSteps.instruction: Gently shift your gaze to a different color and notice its unique features in the same way.

practiceSteps.label: Re-Orient / Allow Experience
practiceSteps.instruction: Remain still for a moment. Notice how your visual perspective feels now.

whatToNotice.text: Visual Depth — Sense the space and perspective between you and the objects.
Colour Richness — Notice the vibrancy and subtle nuances of the colours.
Attentional Focus — Notice how your attention moves from one colour to another.

cards.gentleNote: Move at your own pace. If at any point you feel visual strain, close your eyes for a moment. This practice can be done sitting or standing.
cards.anchor: I can notice what is around me and remain here.

cards.title: The Shape Mapping Reset
cards.invitation: Let your eyes notice the shapes that define your space.
cards.purpose: Visual mapping & environmental awareness. Feel where you are in relation to your surroundings. Use your vision as a form of spatial touch.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Stand or sit in your space. Let your gaze be soft and wide. Notice the overall expanse of the room.

practiceSteps.label: Map Boundaries
practiceSteps.instruction: Visually trace the edges of the room. Notice the lines of the walls, ceiling, and floor.

practiceSteps.label: Locate Shapes
practiceSteps.instruction: Find three specific shapes in the architecture. Notice their dimensions.

practiceSteps.label: Add Objects
practiceSteps.instruction: Locate a piece of furniture or an object. Notice its basic shape and how it sits within the space.

practiceSteps.label: Observe Depth
practiceSteps.instruction: Look between objects. Notice the negative space. Is there a defined path or container?

practiceSteps.label: Follow A Line
practiceSteps.instruction: Choose a long architectural line. Softly follow it with your eyes from start to finish.

practiceSteps.label: Pause
practiceSteps.instruction: Stay for a few slow breaths. Let your eyes move smoothly. Notice the stability.

practiceSteps.label: Release Gaze
practiceSteps.instruction: Gradually soften your focus. Let your eyes return to a neutral gaze, while maintaining a felt sense of the room's geometry.

whatToNotice.text: Boundaries — Are the edges of your space clear or indistinct?
Shapes — What geometric patterns appear in your view?
Spatial Relationships — Can you sense the distance and depth of objects?

cards.gentleNote: Practice on surfaces you trust. This can be adapted to any environment. If you feel visually overwhelmed or motion-sick, pause and refocus on a single stationary object.
cards.anchor: I can see the shape of the space I am in.

cards.title: The Light Anchor
cards.invitation: Notice a steady source of light in the space around you.
cards.purpose: Visual anchoring & environmental orientation. Use a steady light source to stabilize your gaze and spatial awareness.

practiceSteps.label: Locate
practiceSteps.instruction: Look around and select one steady, soft light source, like daylight from a window.

practiceSteps.label: Settle
practiceSteps.instruction: Find a comfortable, natural standing position.

practiceSteps.label: Soften Gaze
practiceSteps.instruction: Direct your eyes to the light and soften your eyes.

practiceSteps.label: Focus
practiceSteps.instruction: Gently maintain visual contact with the light.

practiceSteps.label: Expand Awareness
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice your peripheral vision. What can you still see?

practiceSteps.label: Compare
practiceSteps.instruction: Compare the light to the surrounding space.

practiceSteps.label: Pause
practiceSteps.instruction: Stay with the expanded awareness for several breaths.

whatToNotice.text: Light Quality — The softness, warmth, and steadiness of the light.
Field of Vision — The width of your view, both central and peripheral.
Spatial Calm — The sense of visual stability in your environment.

cards.gentleNote: Focus gently, without intense staring. Keep your vision expansive. If you experience visual strain, look away and take a break.
cards.anchor: I can find a steady point and still see the whole space.

cards.title: The Distance Map
cards.invitation: Notice what is near, what is far, and where you are between them.
cards.purpose: Spatial depth awareness & environmental mapping. Explore your relationship to space and perspective.

practiceSteps.label: Close Focus
practiceSteps.instruction: Stand comfortably and orient to your immediate space. Feel the floor beneath your feet.

practiceSteps.label: Mid Focus
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice something within your reach. Its texture, its color. Feel your physical connection to it.

practiceSteps.label: Distant Focus
practiceSteps.instruction: Look through a window to the furthest point in your field. Observe the light, details far away.

practiceSteps.label: Re-Center
practiceSteps.instruction: Bring attention back to your feet. They are your stable center point.

practiceSteps.label: Trace The Spaces
practiceSteps.instruction: Visually trace the space from you to close, to mid, and to far objects.

practiceSteps.label: Notice The Middle
practiceSteps.instruction: Sense where your body is positioned relative to all these points. Feel the 'between-ness'.

practiceSteps.label: Pause & Reflect
practiceSteps.instruction: Hold this layered spatial awareness for a few slow breaths, sensing the breadth of your environment.

whatToNotice.text: Pressure — How does your grounding feel as your gaze moves between distances?
Position — Can you sense your location relative to the objects around you?
Support — Do you feel more spacious yet connected as you notice your surroundings?

cards.gentleNote: Move at your own pace. Visual tracking can be adapted. If spatial perception feels challenging, start with fewer points. If you experience dizziness or eye strain, reduce the focus points or take a break.
cards.anchor: I can notice where things are and where I am among them.

cards.title: The Visual Return
cards.invitation: Let your attention move away — then come back to the space around you.
cards.purpose: Attentional flexibility & environmental return. Feel where you are. Build awareness of visual spatial.

practiceSteps.label: Find a Vantage Point
practiceSteps.instruction: Stand or sit with a clear view of your surroundings.

practiceSteps.label: Look Away
practiceSteps.instruction: Gaze at a distance, perhaps out a window or at the far wall.

practiceSteps.label: Focus
practiceSteps.instruction: Pick a specific detail at that distance and notice its features.

practiceSteps.label: Sense Your Body
practiceSteps.instruction: While gazing, briefly check-in with your physical grounding.

practiceSteps.label: Shift Focus
practiceSteps.instruction: Slowly bring your gaze back to a nearby object.

practiceSteps.label: Detail
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice a different detail about this close object, like its texture.

practiceSteps.label: Notice Spatial Relations
practiceSteps.instruction: Where are you, relative to these objects?

practiceSteps.label: Repeat
practiceSteps.instruction: Alternate this process a few times.

whatToNotice.text: Sensation — Notice visual-somatic responses, not just the image.
Attention — Can you sense the shift in how your attention is moving?
Clarity — Does the environment seem sharper upon your return?

cards.gentleNote: If you experience eye strain or dizziness, soften your gaze or take a break. Move at your own pace.
cards.anchor: I can move my attention and find my way back.

Flagged for awareness.

cards.title: The Gentle Sway
cards.invitation: Let your body move a little without losing your place.
cards.purpose: Gentle movement & spatial organisation. Explore a small, comfortable side-to-side movement while staying connected to your feet and the surface beneath you. The goal is to notice movement and return rather than create a large or challenging sway.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Stand with your feet comfortably apart. Let your knees remain soft and notice the floor beneath both feet.

practiceSteps.label: Find Your Centre
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice where your weight feels most balanced between your feet. There is no need to make your posture perfectly symmetrical.

practiceSteps.label: Begin to Sway
practiceSteps.instruction: Very gently allow your body weight to move a little toward one side. Keep both feet connected to the floor.

practiceSteps.label: Move Back Through Centre
practiceSteps.instruction: Allow your weight to travel back toward the middle. Notice the moment when your weight feels more evenly distributed again.

practiceSteps.label: Sway to the Other Side
practiceSteps.instruction: Move slowly toward the opposite side. Keep the movement small enough that you remain comfortable and oriented.

practiceSteps.label: Continue Gently
practiceSteps.instruction: Repeat the side-to-side movement several times. Let the movement remain easy and unhurried.

practiceSteps.label: Return to Stillness
practiceSteps.instruction: Gradually reduce the movement until you are standing quietly again. Notice your feet and the space around you.

whatToNotice.text: Weight — Where do you feel your weight moving?
Support — Can you remain aware of the floor while you move?
Return — What happens when your body comes back toward centre?

cards.gentleNote: Keep the movement smaller than you think you need. Hold a stable surface if balance is uncertain, or practise seated if standing does not feel appropriate. If you experience dizziness, nausea, pain, or significant discomfort, stop and return to a stable position.
cards.anchor: I can move and still find my centre.

cards.title: The Seated Rock
cards.invitation: Explore small movement while something steady supports you.
cards.purpose: Supported movement & positional awareness. Explore small, forward and back movements while your body is supported by a sturdy chair. The goal is to notice the gentle shift and return without straining, using the chair for stability.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Sit on a sturdy chair with feet flat on the floor. Allow your hands to rest on your lap. Notice your foundation.

practiceSteps.label: Find Your Centre
practiceSteps.instruction: Align your posture so your weight feels even on your sit bones. There is no need for perfect symmetry, just comfort.

practiceSteps.label: Begin to Rock Forward
practiceSteps.instruction: Gently lean your upper body forward, allowing your weight to shift from your sit bones towards your knees. Keep your feet in contact with the floor.

practiceSteps.label: Move Back Through Centre
practiceSteps.instruction: Allow your weight to travel back toward the middle, returning to a balanced upright seated position.

practiceSteps.label: Rock Backward
practiceSteps.instruction: Gently lean your upper body backward slightly, allowing your weight to shift towards the back of your sit bones. Maintain foot contact.

practiceSteps.label: Continue Gently
practiceSteps.instruction: Repeat the slow forward and back rocking motion several times, keeping it small and controlled.

practiceSteps.label: Return to Stillness
practiceSteps.instruction: Gradually reduce the movement until you are sitting quietly again. Notice your contact points with the chair and floor.

whatToNotice.text: Weight — Where do you feel your weight moving on your seat?
Support — Can you remain aware of the chair's support while you move?
Return — What happens when your body comes back toward centre?

cards.gentleNote: Keep the movement smaller than you think you need. Do not strain. Focus on subtle sensation. If you experience dizziness, nausea, pain, or significant discomfort, stop and return to a stable, neutral seated position.
cards.anchor: I can move and still find my centre.

cards.title: The Centre-Line Return
cards.invitation: Move away from centre — then notice your way back.
cards.purpose: Postural orientation & return to centre. Explore gentle movement away from midline, then focus on the sensory awareness of precisely returning to your vertical axis. This develops spatial organisation and stability.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Stand with feet comfortably apart.

practiceSteps.label: Find Centre
practiceSteps.instruction: Distribute weight evenly.

practiceSteps.label: Initiate Shift
practiceSteps.instruction: Gently shift weight to one side.

practiceSteps.label: Notice Change
practiceSteps.instruction: Observe the feet and base.

practiceSteps.label: Return to Centre
practiceSteps.instruction: Slowly bring weight back.

practiceSteps.label: Sense the Return
practiceSteps.instruction: Feel the midline re-engaging.

practiceSteps.label: Repeat & Observe
practiceSteps.instruction: Alternate sides, notice returns.

practiceSteps.label: Final Stillness
practiceSteps.instruction: Come to a still centre.

whatToNotice.text: Weight — Where do you feel weight shifting back?
Support — Can you feel the support of the floor as you cross centre?
Return — Describe the sensation of finding your exact midline.

cards.gentleNote: Keep the initial movement very small. Focus on the sensory return. This practice is not about the sway, but about the return to alignment. If balance is a concern, hold a surface. If discomfort arises, please stop and rest.
cards.anchor: I can move and still find my centre.

cards.title: The Slow Turn
cards.invitation: Turn slowly and let your body update with the movement.
cards.purpose: Explore a controlled, full-body rotation. Notice how your sense of space and orientation updates with each degree of movement. The goal is a seamless update of your inner map, not a fast spin.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive & Ground
practiceSteps.instruction: Stand with your feet comfortably apart. Sense the floor beneath you. Soften your knees.

practiceSteps.label: Choose a Reference Point
practiceSteps.instruction: Select a clear visual object or point in front of you as your starting orientation.

practiceSteps.label: Begin the Rotation
practiceSteps.instruction: Start a very slow, controlled turn towards one side (e.g., right), keeping your body integrated.

practiceSteps.label: Lead With Your Intention
practiceSteps.instruction: Direct your attention to the destination. Let the turn originate from your core.

practiceSteps.label: Let Your Head Follow
practiceSteps.instruction: Your head should naturally rotate with your spine, keeping your eyes updated.

practiceSteps.label: Continue Gently
practiceSteps.instruction: Turn as far as is comfortable and controlled. The key is to avoid jerky movements.

practiceSteps.label: Update Your Map
practiceSteps.instruction: As you turn, mentally update the positions of objects around you in your spatial awareness.

practiceSteps.label: Return to Stillness
practiceSteps.instruction: Slow the turn to a stop. Face your original reference point or a new one. Recalibrate your sense of 'front'.

whatToNotice.text: Weight — Where is the pressure in your feet shifting as you rotate?
Support — How does your central balance line feel during rotation?
Return — How does it feel to return your gaze to your starting point?

cards.gentleNote: Practice on a stable surface. Use small, partial turns initially to build control. If turning triggers vertigo or significant imbalance, reduce the degree of turn or practice seated, turning your head and torso.
cards.anchor: I can rotate my view and still return to my center.

cards.title: The Weight-Transfer Reset
cards.invitation: Feel your weight move from one foot to the other.
cards.purpose: Weight transfer & balance awareness. Learn to consciously shift weight from foot to foot while maintaining connection and awareness. The goal is a controlled, mindful transfer rather than a fast or unstable move.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Stand with your feet comfortably apart. Let your knees remain soft and notice the floor beneath both feet.

practiceSteps.label: Find Your Centre
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice where your weight feels most balanced between your feet. There is no need to make your posture perfectly symmetrical.

practiceSteps.label: Initiate Weight Shift
practiceSteps.instruction: Very gently, allow your weight to begin to move towards one foot. Keep the other foot still connected.

practiceSteps.label: Deepen The Shift
practiceSteps.instruction: Allow more weight to settle on the chosen foot.

practiceSteps.label: Notice Pressure
practiceSteps.instruction: Feel the increased pressure under the supporting foot.

practiceSteps.label: Release And Return
practiceSteps.instruction: Slow down, release the weight and allow it to drift back towards the centre.

practiceSteps.label: Shift To Other Side
practiceSteps.instruction: Repeat the shift to the opposite foot, slowly.

practiceSteps.label: Return To Balance
practiceSteps.instruction: Gradually reduce the shifts, finding a neutral, balanced stance.

whatToNotice.text: Weight — Where do you feel your weight moving?
Support — Can you remain aware of the floor while you move?
Return — What happens when your body comes back toward centre?

cards.gentleNote: Keep the movement smaller than you think you need. Hold a stable surface if balance is uncertain, or practise seated if standing does not feel appropriate. If you experience dizziness, nausea, pain, or significant discomfort, stop and return to a stable position.
cards.anchor: I can transfer weight and remain perfectly grounded.

cards.title: The Head-Level Reset
cards.invitation: Move gently while keeping your head oriented.
cards.purpose: Head position & movement organisation. Explore head and eye organization during a gentle body shift. Keep your head level and oriented while the rest of your body moves. The goal is to notice stability in your visual field and return rather than create a large head turn.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Stand comfortably with feet apart. Let your knees remain soft and notice the floor beneath both feet.

practiceSteps.label: Find Your Centre
practiceSteps.instruction: Feel your weight balanced. Gaze softly ahead at a single point (or the horizon).

practiceSteps.label: Soften Gaze
practiceSteps.instruction: Maintain a soft gaze at your focal point. Notice the visual field around you.

practiceSteps.label: Shift Weight
practiceSteps.instruction: Very gently allow your body weight to move toward one side. Keep your head level.

practiceSteps.label: Maintain Orientation
practiceSteps.instruction: Challenge yourself to keep your head from tilting or turning as you shift.

practiceSteps.label: Move Through Centre
practiceSteps.instruction: Move back to centre and then to the other foot, keeping your head level.

practiceSteps.label: Return to Stillness
practiceSteps.instruction: Gradually stop the shift. Return to standing with head level and centered. Notice how it feels.

whatToNotice.text: Weight — Where do you feel your weight moving? Is your head still?
Support — Are your feet still well-connected to the floor?
Return — How easily can you find center and head orientation?

cards.gentleNote: Keep the movement smaller than you think you need. Hold a stable surface if balance is uncertain, or practise seated if standing does not feel appropriate. If you experience dizziness, nausea, pain, or significant discomfort, stop and return to a stable position.
cards.anchor: I can move and still find my centre.

cards.title: The Step-and-Settle
cards.invitation: Take one small step — then let your body find the floor again.
cards.purpose: Movement transition & spatial confidence. Feel the moment of release between efforts.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Stand with feet hip-width. Notice your initial stability.

practiceSteps.label: Weight Shift
practiceSteps.instruction: Slowly shift your weight onto one leg. Feel your new base.

practiceSteps.label: Lift
practiceSteps.instruction: Gradually peel the other foot off the floor, lifting the knee slightly.

practiceSteps.label: Extend
practiceSteps.instruction: Reach the lifted leg forward or to the side, maintaining balance.

practiceSteps.label: Place
practiceSteps.instruction: Gently place the foot on the floor. Make contact heel-to-ball.

practiceSteps.label: Settle
practiceSteps.instruction: Full weight transfer. Allow your body weight to fully drop into the new base.

practiceSteps.label: Notice
practiceSteps.instruction: Stay for a full breath. Observe the change in support and stability.

practiceSteps.label: Repeat
practiceSteps.instruction: Lift the previous support foot and bring it to meet the first, or step with the other.

whatToNotice.text: Pressure — What sensations do you feel as weight transfers?
Position — Can you sense your body's geometry in motion?
Support — How does the floor feel 'rising up' to meet you?

cards.gentleNote: Move slowly, with curiosity. This can be adapted to sitting by taking a small step from a seated position. If you experience balance issues or dizziness, reduce the size of the step or take a break. Consult a somatic practitioner.
cards.anchor: I have rhythm. I can find balance in transition. I can be steady.

cards.title: The Upright Return
cards.invitation: Notice how your body finds an upright position again.
cards.purpose: Postural transition & bodily organisation. Feel the natural ease of rising. Move with intentional stability.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Stand near a low stool or seated on a low cushion. Settle into your base and notice your breath.

practiceSteps.label: Engage
practiceSteps.instruction: Shift your weight toward your feet. Feel your lower body activate.

practiceSteps.label: Activate
practiceSteps.instruction: Push gently into the floor through your feet.

practiceSteps.label: Rise
practiceSteps.instruction: Continue the movement, rising from the low position.

practiceSteps.label: Upright
practiceSteps.instruction: Achieve a natural, relaxed, tall standing posture.

practiceSteps.label: Center
practiceSteps.instruction: Pause in this upright position. Focus gently on a stable horizon.

practiceSteps.label: Integrate
practiceSteps.instruction: Stay for a few breaths. Release unnecessary tension.

whatToNotice.text: Pressure — What do you feel where your hands and feet make contact?
Position — Can you sense where your body is in space?
Support — What changes when you allow the surface to hold some of your weight?

cards.gentleNote: Move with a sense of ease, not speed. If you feel unstable or lightheaded, take a moment and re-establish your base.
cards.anchor: I have weight. I can create pressure. I can be supported.

cards.title: The Supported Balance Pause
cards.invitation: Let support be part of how you balance.
cards.purpose: Supported balance & stability awareness. Sense how external support can help you feel stable.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Stand clear. Initial body scan.

practiceSteps.label: Contact
practiceSteps.instruction: Reach out. Touch the countertop.

practiceSteps.label: Shift Weight
practiceSteps.instruction: Lean subtly. Feel weight distribute.

practiceSteps.label: Find Balance
practiceSteps.instruction: Lift a foot. Discover new points of connection.

practiceSteps.label: Pause & Observe
practiceSteps.instruction: Hold the pose. Notice sensations.

practiceSteps.label: Engage Core
practiceSteps.instruction: Connect core muscles. Increase inner support.

practiceSteps.label: Release Hand
practiceSteps.instruction: Temporarily lift your hand. Test your own balance.

practiceSteps.label: Return to Stance
practiceSteps.instruction: Step down. Standard standing pose.

whatToNotice.text: Pressure — What do you feel where your hand and foot make contact?
Position — Can you sense your center of gravity shifting?
Support — How does the countertop support your feeling of stability?

cards.gentleNote: Move with intention. Ensure the countertop is sturdy and will not move. If you feel unbalanced or dizzy, stop and rest immediately. Adapt to a seated balance pose if needed.
cards.anchor: I can sense support. My body finds balance. I am steady and organized.

cards.title: The Movement-to-Stillness Reset
cards.invitation: Move gently — then notice what happens when you stop.
cards.purpose: Transition from movement to stillness. Find calmness through controlled release.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Stand with feet hip-width. Soft knees. Take 3 deep breaths.

practiceSteps.label: Start
practiceSteps.instruction: Introduce gentle swaying from side to side. Micro-movements in the feet.

practiceSteps.label: Expand
practiceSteps.instruction: Slowly let the sway grow larger, engaging the hips.

practiceSteps.label: Add Arms
practiceSteps.instruction: Gently float arms up and down, like in water.

practiceSteps.label: Flow
practiceSteps.instruction: Move freely and comfortably for one minute. Find a rhythm.

practiceSteps.label: Slow Down
practiceSteps.instruction: Gradually reduce the size and speed of all movement.

practiceSteps.label: Almost Still
practiceSteps.instruction: Movements become almost imperceptible, internal only.

practiceSteps.label: Still
practiceSteps.instruction: Come to a complete physical stop. Notice the absence of outward motion.

whatToNotice.text: Sensation — What do you feel where your feet make contact? Feel the full sole.
Balance — Can you sense your center of gravity? Are you shifting or centered?
Internal Shifts — What is moving internally now that the outside is still? Find micro-pulsations.

cards.gentleNote: Move at your own pace. Use a stable, secure surface. This practice can be adapted to sitting if needed. If you experience pain or dizziness, reduce the pressure or take a break.
cards.anchor: I have movement. I have stillness. I can integrate them. I can find calm.

cards.title: The Texture Return
cards.invitation: Let your skin notice what it is touching.
cards.purpose: Tactile awareness & sensory discrimination. Use a familiar object with a distinct texture to explore how your skin receives information through contact. Rather than trying to create a particular sensation, notice qualities such as smoothness, roughness, softness, firmness, and temperature.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Sit comfortably and let your hands rest for a moment. Notice the contact between your hands and whatever is supporting them.

practiceSteps.label: Choose an Object
practiceSteps.instruction: Select a safe, familiar object with a noticeable texture — a soft cloth, smooth stone, wooden object, towel, or another everyday item.

practiceSteps.label: Make Contact
practiceSteps.instruction: Place your fingertips or palm gently against the object. Begin with light contact rather than gripping or pressing firmly.

practiceSteps.label: Notice the Texture
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice what the surface feels like. Is it smooth, rough, soft, firm, coarse, ridged, or somewhere between?

practiceSteps.label: Explore Slowly
practiceSteps.instruction: If comfortable, move your fingertips or palm slowly across the surface. Notice whether the sensation changes as your contact moves.

practiceSteps.label: Change the Pressure
practiceSteps.instruction: Very gently vary the amount of pressure. Notice the difference between light contact and slightly firmer contact.

practiceSteps.label: Compare
practiceSteps.instruction: Pause and compare what you noticed with the object held still versus when your hand was moving across it.

practiceSteps.label: Return
practiceSteps.instruction: Place your hand back on the object without moving. Let the texture become familiar again, then gradually release contact.

practiceSteps.label: Notice Your Hand
practiceSteps.instruction: After letting go, notice your hand for a few moments. What sensations remain — temperature, tingling, pressure, or simply the absence of contact?

whatToNotice.text: Texture — What qualities can your skin distinguish?
Pressure — How does the sensation change when contact becomes lighter or firmer?
Change — What do you notice when your hand moves compared with when it stays still?

cards.gentleNote: Choose an object that feels safe and comfortable to touch. There is no need to use a strong texture or press firmly. Keep the exploration within a comfortable range and stop if the sensation becomes unpleasant, painful, overwhelming, or irritating. You can practise with clothing or another familiar surface if direct contact with an object does not feel comfortable.
cards.anchor: I can notice sensation and choose how I make contact.

cards.title: The Temperature Shift
cards.invitation: Notice how temperature changes through contact.
cards.purpose: Thermal awareness & sensory comparison. Learn to differentiate and notice subtle differences in temperature between skin and objects, and how these sensations evolve with contact. Rather than judging as "hot" or "cold," explore the gradient and rate of thermal transfer.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Sit comfortably and let your hands test for a moment. Notice the contact between your hands and whatever is supporting them.

practiceSteps.label: Select Objects
practiceSteps.instruction: Select two safe everyday objects known to hold different temperatures (e.g., a warm ceramic mug and a polished stone). Place them close.

practiceSteps.label: Make Neutral Contact
practiceSteps.instruction: Gently place your palms against both surfaces. Notice the initial temperature difference.

practiceSteps.label: Explore One Surface
practiceSteps.instruction: Focus only on one object (e.g., the warm mug). Notice the quality of the warmth. How deep does it feel?

practiceSteps.label: Explore The Other
practiceSteps.instruction: Shift focus to the cool stone. Notice the quality of the coolness. Is it sharp or diffuse?

practiceSteps.label: Notice Shifts
practiceSteps.instruction: Hold both hands still for a few moments. Notice how the sensations of warmth and coolness change. Does one hand warm the object, or the object cool the hand?

practiceSteps.label: Compare & Repeat
practiceSteps.instruction: Pause and compare the sensations before and after contact. Let the objects return to their neutral states before repeating.

whatToNotice.text: Thermal Gradient — What is the specific 'flavor' of warmth or coolness? How does it differ across the skin?
Rate of Transfer — How quickly does the sensation change? Notice how your body's temperature reacts.
Comparison — How does the memory of the cold sensation affect your perception of the warm one?

cards.gentleNote: Choose safe objects. Do not use items that are burning hot or freezing cold. Focus on gentle, palpable differences. If discomfort occurs, stop. Keep exploration comfortable.
cards.anchor: I can notice temperature sensation and choose how I interact.

cards.title: The Cool Contact Reset
cards.invitation: Explore a cool sensation without making it intense.
cards.purpose: Tactile awareness & sensory discrimination. Use a familiar object with a distinct texture to explore how your skin receives information through contact. Rather than trying to create a particular sensation, notice qualities such as smoothness, roughness, softness, firmness, and temperature.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Sit comfortably and let your hands rest for a moment. Notice the ambient temperature on your skin.

practiceSteps.label: Choose an Object
practiceSteps.instruction: Select a safe, cool object with a noticeable difference in temperature — a smooth, cool stone, a damp cool cloth, or a metal spoon.

practiceSteps.label: Make Contact
practiceSteps.instruction: Place your fingertips or palm gently against the cool surface. Begin with light contact.

practiceSteps.label: Notice the Temperature
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice what the surface temperature feels like. Is it distinctly cold, merely cool, or closer to room temperature?

practiceSteps.label: Explore Slowly
practiceSteps.instruction: If comfortable, move your fingertips or palm slowly across the cool surface. Notice whether the temperature sensation changes as your contact moves.

practiceSteps.label: Change the Pressure
practiceSteps.instruction: Very gently vary the amount of pressure. Notice how increasing pressure affects the perception of coolness.

practiceSteps.label: Compare
practiceSteps.instruction: Pause and compare what you noticed with the object held still versus when your hand was moving across it.

whatToNotice.text: Temperature — What qualities can your skin distinguish?
Pressure — How does the sensation change when contact becomes lighter or firmer?
Change — What do you notice when your hand moves compared with when it stays still?

cards.gentleNote: Choose an object that feels safe and comfortable to touch. There is no need to use extreme temperatures. Keep exploration within a comfortable range. You can practise with a damp cloth, a smooth stone, or a metal object if preferred. If direct cold contact feels uncomfortable, use a thin barrier cloth.
cards.anchor: I can notice sensation and choose how I make contact.

cards.title: The Warmth Return
cards.invitation: Notice warmth, then notice what changes when contact ends.
cards.purpose: Warmth awareness & sensory return. Use a safe, pre-warmed object (like a folded, warm cloth) to explore how your skin registers temperature and how that comforting sensation is perceived and how it lingers after the object is removed.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Sit comfortably and let your hands rest. Notice the contact between your hands and whatever supports them.

practiceSteps.label: Choose a Warm Object
practiceSteps.instruction: Select a safe, pre-warmed object (e.g., a warm, dry washcloth, a safe warm stone, a comfortable pre-heated fabric item).

practiceSteps.label: Initial Contact
practiceSteps.instruction: Gently place your palm or fingertips against the warm object. Start with light, light contact.

practiceSteps.label: Registering Warmth
practiceSteps.instruction: Focus only on the warmth. Notice how it feels — comfortable, soothing, deep, or stable.

practiceSteps.label: Sustained Contact
practiceSteps.instruction: Keep the contact stable for 1-2 minutes. Feel the warmth deepening into the tissues.

practiceSteps.label: Gradual Release
practiceSteps.instruction: Very slowly and mindfully, begin to lift your hand away from the object, noticing the exact moment direct contact ends.

practiceSteps.label: Compare Sensations
practiceSteps.instruction: Compare what you noticed with the object held still versus when your hand was moving across it.

practiceSteps.label: Notice the Aftermath
practiceSteps.instruction: With your hand held still, notice any lingering sensations — warmth, tingling, or subtle changes in feel.

whatToNotice.text: Sensation — What is the quality of the warmth? (Sustained, comforting, radiant)
Gradient — How does the sensation change as contact persists or eases?
The After-Effect — What sensations remain in your skin after the object is gone?

cards.gentleNote: Select an object with a safe, comfortable level of warmth. Do not use items that are hot enough to burn or cause distress. A slightly pre-warmed cloth is ideal. If you have temperature sensitivities, practice with caution.
cards.anchor: I can notice and hold the feeling of comfort and warmth, even after the source is gone.

cards.title: The Forearm Sweep
cards.invitation: Let your skin notice the difference between contact and movement.
cards.purpose: Tactile movement & sensory mapping. Using deliberate movement to map skin sensitivity and note how tactile input changes with motion.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Sit comfortably and let your arms rest. Notice the contact between your arm and whatever is supporting it.

practiceSteps.label: Prepare the Arm
practiceSteps.instruction: Extend one forearm comfortably, palms-up.

practiceSteps.label: Light Contact
practiceSteps.instruction: Place your other hand's fingertips (or palm) gently on the wrist of the extended forearm. Begin with very light contact.

practiceSteps.label: Move Slowly
practiceSteps.instruction: Very slowly, sweep your hand up the forearm toward the elbow. Notice the movement itself.

practiceSteps.label: Notice Sensation
practiceSteps.instruction: What does the contact feel like as it moves? Is it constant, changing, smooth, or discontinuous?

practiceSteps.label: Compare Speed
practiceSteps.instruction: Try a faster sweep, then slow down. Notice the difference in sensation at different speeds.

practiceSteps.label: Stillness & Return
practiceSteps.instruction: Place your hand still on the forearm. Notice the sensation in stillness. Then return your hands to rest.

whatToNotice.text: Texture — How does movement help you define the texture and contours of your forearm?
Pressure — Does changing speed affect how pressure is perceived at different points?
Change — What specific changes in sensation do you feel with motion versus static contact?

cards.gentleNote: Choose a time when you are calm and free from distraction. You can practice with clothing or another surface if direct skin contact is uncomfortable.
cards.anchor: I can notice sensation and choose how I make contact.
