cards.title: The Containment Hold
cards.invitation: Feel the boundary of your body through chosen contact.
cards.purpose: Tactile awareness & self-boundary definition. Use specific self-contact points to explore the edges of your physical form. Create a sense of containment and safe boundary without gripping. Focus on the sensation of being held by yourself.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Sit comfortably and let your hands rest for a moment. Notice the contact between your hands and whatever supports them.

practiceSteps.label: Choose a Contact
practiceSteps.instruction: Select a safe, comfortable area of your own body that feels comfortable for contact — the opposite upper arm, shoulder, or chest.

practiceSteps.label: Make Contact
practiceSteps.instruction: Place one hand (the holding hand) gently but firmly against the chosen area (the held area). Use a supportive, enveloping touch.

practiceSteps.label: Feel the Boundary
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice the sensation. How does your skin receive the pressure from your hand? Can you trace the edge where your hand and body meet?

practiceSteps.label: Notice the Containee
practiceSteps.instruction: Become aware of the sensation of being held. How does the area under your hand feel contained or defined?

practiceSteps.label: Slowly Release
practiceSteps.instruction: Maintain the awareness. Very gradually, reduce the pressure until your hand makes only light contact, then slowly lift it away completely.

practiceSteps.label: Compare
practiceSteps.instruction: After letting go, notice how your body and awareness feel now. Does the area feel more defined or settled? Compare it with the other side.

whatToNotice.text: Boundary — How defined or contained does your physical body feel under contact?
Pressure — How does the sense of containment change with contact?
Change — How does the sense of containment change when contact stays still?

cards.gentleNote: Choose areas that feel safe and comfortable to hold. Avoid any areas of tension or pain. If self-contact is not comfortable, you can practice with a blanket or pillow for the sensation of containment. Keep the exploration within a pleasant and defining range.
cards.anchor: I can create my own sense of safety and defined boundary through my touch.

cards.title: The Pressure Choice Practice
cards.invitation: Explore how much pressure feels right for you. Regulate your sensory experience.
cards.purpose: Pressure discrimination & sensory choice. Explore how different pressures feel to discover your ideal sensation and foster choice.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Find a stable, soft-textured cushion. Sit or stand comfortably and let your shoulders soften.

practiceSteps.label: Light Contact
practiceSteps.instruction: Place one palm very gently against the cushion, as light as a feather. Just rest it there.

practiceSteps.label: Increase
practiceSteps.instruction: Slowly and carefully increase the pressure of your palm, noticing the resistance.

practiceSteps.label: Sustain
practiceSteps.instruction: Hold the pressure at a level that feels firm but still comfortable. Notice the sensation.

practiceSteps.label: Reduce
practiceSteps.instruction: Slowly begin to ease off the pressure. Feel the moment the tension recedes.

practiceSteps.label: Pause
practiceSteps.instruction: Pause at a lower, but still present, pressure. Stay for a few breaths.

practiceSteps.label: Compare & Choose
practiceSteps.instruction: Move back and forth between light and firm pressure, noticing which feels more supportive.

whatToNotice.text: Touch Clarity — What do you feel where your hands and feet make contact?
Tactile Range — What can sense where your body is in space with this difference?
Choice and Comfort — What changes when choice and comfort?

cards.gentleNote: Move at your own pace. Use a stable, secure surface. This practice can be adapted to sitting if needed. If you experience pain or dizziness, reduce the pressure or take a break.
cards.anchor: I can notice subtle differences. I have a choice in how I engage with pressure.

cards.title: The Hand-to-Arm Contact
cards.invitation: Notice one part of your body through the contact of another.
cards.purpose: Self-touch & localisation. Feel your own presence. Define boundaries and edges.

practiceSteps.label: Arrive
practiceSteps.instruction: Find a comfortable seated or standing position. Soften your shoulders.

practiceSteps.label: Place
practiceSteps.instruction: Gently place one palm (the 'touching' hand) on the forearm of your other arm.

practiceSteps.label: Contact
practiceSteps.instruction: Bring your attention to the meeting point of the two surfaces.

practiceSteps.label: Sense
practiceSteps.instruction: Notice the initial sensation. Is the contact warm or cool? Dry or moist?

practiceSteps.label: Discriminate
practiceSteps.instruction: Compare the sensation on the palm with the sensation on the forearm.

practiceSteps.label: Pause
practiceSteps.instruction: Hold the position. Breathe slowly. Let the sensations deepen.

practiceSteps.label: Release
practiceSteps.instruction: Gradually and slowly lift the touching hand. Notice the trailing sensation.

whatToNotice.text: Temperature — Which part of your contact feels warmer? The hand or the forearm?
Texture & Pressure — Can you sense the different skin textures? Is there a sense of deep pressure?
Boundaries & Limits — Where does your touching hand end and the receiving arm begin?

cards.gentleNote: Move at your own pace. Let curiosity guide you, not force. If any sensation is uncomfortable, decrease pressure or take a break.
cards.anchor: I have skin. I can feel temperature. I can define my boundaries.

cards.title: The Thermal Map
cards.invitation: Notice where warmth and coolness appear across your body.
cards.purpose: Thermal localisation & sensory mapping. Feel temperature shifts and create a full-body map.

practiceSteps.label: Locate
practiceSteps.instruction: Rest your hands on a neutral surface. Observe the current temperature.

practiceSteps.label: Explore
practiceSteps.instruction: Shift your focus to another area, like your face. Is it warmer or cooler than your hands?

practiceSteps.label: Compare
practiceSteps.instruction: Contrast two distant areas. Notice the difference between your right palm and your left thigh.

practiceSteps.label: Track
practiceSteps.instruction: Trace the flow of temperature shifts over your skin as they move.

practiceSteps.label: Map
practiceSteps.instruction: Become aware of multiple temperature zones simultaneously, building a complete picture.

practiceSteps.label: Ground
practiceSteps.instruction: Use the clearest feeling of warmth or coolness as a sensory anchor to ground yourself.

whatToNotice.text: Zone Focus — Identify one distinct area of temperature (warm or cool).
Contrast Scan — Shift attention to a differing temperature zone and notice the contrast.
Full Body Map — Perceive multiple zones at once and see the full bodily thermal landscape.

cards.gentleNote: Move at your own pace. Use a stable, secure surface. This practice can be adapted to sitting if needed. If you experience pain or dizziness, reduce the pressure or take a break.
cards.anchor: My body is a landscape of feeling. I can track the change.

cards.title: The Texture Discrimination Map
cards.invitation: Notice how many different qualities your skin can distinguish.
cards.purpose: Tactile comparison & sensory precision. Compare surfaces. Distinguish fine details through touch.

practiceSteps.label: Prepare
practiceSteps.instruction: Quiet your space. Position hands comfortably.

practiceSteps.label: Gather Samples
practiceSteps.instruction: Select three distinctly different textured objects.

practiceSteps.label: Initial Touch
practiceSteps.instruction: Gently touch one surface with a single fingertip.

practiceSteps.label: Compare Surfaces
practiceSteps.instruction: Alternately touch other samples with the same finger.

practiceSteps.label: Explore Detail
practiceSteps.instruction: Use small, slow circular motions to feel surface features.

practiceSteps.label: Focus
practiceSteps.instruction: Close your eyes to sharpen texture sensations.

practiceSteps.label: Notice
practiceSteps.instruction: Sense roughness, smoothness, coolness, or warmth.

practiceSteps.label: Reflect
practiceSteps.instruction: Note how the sensations feel to your skin.

whatToNotice.text: Fine Texture — What small details can your skin detect?
Thermal — Do surfaces feel cool, warm, or neutral?
Friction — How easily does your skin glide across the surface?

cards.gentleNote: Move with curiosity. Use various skin parts (fingertips, palm). If any sensation feels uncomfortable, discontinue.
cards.anchor: I can sense distinction. I can explore surface. I am perceptive.
